Assets & operations

Harper Basin, offshore Liberia.

Exploring 8,924 km² of undrilled deepwater Cretaceous basin floor fans alongside operator TotalEnergies.

1. The play: Cretaceous basin floor fan complexes

The Harper Basin is a transform margin basin located in ultra-deep waters off southern Liberia, representing one of the few remaining lightly explored Cretaceous turbidite fan provinces along the West African Equatorial margin.

Regional legacy seismic interpretation across Blocks LB-26, LB-30, and LB-31 has identified seven discrete Cretaceous basin floor fan systems. These fans exhibit high-amplitude stratigraphic seismic anomalies analogous to major commercial petroleum discoveries in Ghana (Jubilee, TEN), Côte d'Ivoire (Baleine, Calao), and the conjugate margin in Guyana and Suriname.

Thick marine shale sequences provide both rich Cenomanian-Turonian oil-prone source kitchens and regional top seals, while coarse submarine channel-fan sand bodies provide high-porosity reservoir intervals.

Geological Cross-Section Model: Schematic representation of Cretaceous stratigraphic fan pinch-outs against continental slope shales with deepwater wellbore penetration trajectory.

2. The partnership: Joint exploration with TotalEnergies

In January 2026, BluEnergies formalized a Joint Study and Assessment Agreement (JSAA) with energy supermajor TotalEnergies covering Reconnaissance Licence RL-003.

Reconnaissance Licence RL-003 was granted by the Liberia Petroleum Regulatory Authority (LPRA) and encompasses 8,924 km² (approx. 2.2 million acres) across ultra-deepwater blocks LB-26, LB-30, and LB-31.

Under the agreement, TotalEnergies holds 65% operating interest and BluEnergies holds 35% participating interest. The licence term remains valid through 30 June 2027. Significantly, all approved exploration expenditures incurred during the reconnaissance term are eligible for recovery upon transitioning to petroleum sharing contracts.

3. The work programme: Modern seismic & seabed surveys

BluEnergies and TotalEnergies are executing a comprehensive multi-phase technical campaign designed to mature high-grade geological prospects into drill-ready well targets.

3D Seismic Reprocessing

International geophysical contractor TGS ASA is actively reprocessing 6,167 km² of modern 3D seismic data. Advanced broadband processing routines and amplitude-versus-offset (AVO) modeling are being applied to delineate reservoir geometry, resolve stratigraphic trapping mechanisms, and evaluate Direct Hydrocarbon Indicators (DHIs).

Multibeam & Seabed Coring

In partnership with GeoPartners and TDI-Brooks utilizing the research vessel R/V GYRE, a 4,045 km² high-resolution Multibeam Echosounder (MBES) bathymetric survey is under way. The survey maps seafloor topography, detects active hydrocarbon seepage anomalies, and performs piston coring and heat flow measurements to calibrate thermal maturity models.

Path to drilling decisions

The integrated outputs from 3D reprocessing, seabed seepage coring, and thermal gradient analysis will directly support the refinement of drillable prospect candidates and the formal selection of well locations ahead of licence term conversion.
